description: Server-owned failure notices for failed Slack-origin turns with an expiring, signed, actor- and context-bound Retry action verified at the existing interaction boundary, and a durable, recoverable fresh execution attempt (root re-launch or force-new-turn follow-up) that converges on exactly one attempt across replay, redelivery, concurrency, and restart.

tasks.title: Extend terminal delivery contracts and render the Server-owned failure notice
tasks.description: Extend SlackTerminalDelivery additively with optional sessionId/inputId/turnId and failure facts: initial-launch events (AgentJobLineage.BuildTerminalDeliveryEnvelope) stamp identity from AgentJobInput, follow-up events (AgentSessionGrain.TryEmitFollowupDeliveryAsync) stamp turn ids and the currently-hardcoded-null failure reason/category. SlackTerminalDeliveryHandler consumes both event kinds for status failed and renders one Server-owned failure notice via a new SlackStatusProjection.EnqueueExplicitFailureAsync (outbox kind ExplicitFailure, dispatch key slack-failure:{sessionId}:{turnId}, legacy slack-failure:{jobKey}) in the originating conversation/thread, presenting only sanitized reason/category/next-step facts through the existing redaction pipeline. Legacy events without identity render text-only; Manager (Mohist App) deliveries render text-only; reaction closeout (FinalizeLivenessAsync) and Agent reply-action promotion stay unchanged (design A, K).
acceptanceCriteria: A failed Slack-origin initial launch (terminal-delivery event, status failed) posts a failure notice in the originating conversation/thread stating sanitized reason, category when known, and a next step — verified by a spec test under packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.SpecTests/Specs/Slack/
A failed follow-up turn (followup-delivery event) renders the same sanitized notice shape in the same thread — spec test

Notice text is produced through the terminal redaction/summary pipeline: a test feeding raw provider errors, credentials, endpoints, and stack traces asserts none are reproduced verbatim and text length is bounded
The notice uses its own outbox dispatch key and never promotes, embeds, or overwrites the Agent reply row; a test proves reply-action delivery and the notice coexist without dispatch-key contention

New terminal-delivery events carry sessionId, inputId, turnId, and failureCategory; a JSON round-trip test shows legacy events (missing fields) deserialize tolerantly and still render a readable text-only notice with no Retry control
Manager (Mohist App) failure deliveries render a text-only notice with no Retry control — spec test
Existing FinalizeLivenessAsync reaction-closeout behavior and terminal liveness suites remain green (regression)
tasks.output: Extended SlackTerminalDelivery contract (AgentJobLineage.cs, AgentSessionGrain.SlackDelivery.cs), SlackTerminalDeliveryHandler failure branch, SlackStatusProjection.EnqueueExplicitFailureAsync with ExplicitFailure outbox kind, and new Specs/Slack failure-notice spec suites
tasks.notes: Nullable fields + JSON-tolerant deserialization keep old events and old readers compatible in both directions (design K). No Retry control is attached in this task; the notice is the terminal explicit-failure projection replacing reaction-only closeout.

tasks.title: Retryability matrix and signed Retry action attached to retryable failure notices
tasks.description: Add a static, code-owned classifier (SlackFailureRetryPolicy, beside the EventCatalog failure-category vocabulary) mapping the authoritative failure category to retryable/not-retryable (retryable: runner-unavailable, runner-lost, report-timeout, timeout/deadline, transport, rate-limit; never retryable: category-less, unknown, legacy, input/configuration/permission, context exhaustion) and deriving the per-class next-step copy. Extract the canonical-form + HMAC-SHA256 + FixedTimeEquals signing helpers from SlackTurnControlService into a shared implementation used by both Stop and the new mohist_retry_turn action (v1 SlackRetryActionPayload binding failed session/input/turn identity, actor and initiator user ids, connection, team, conversation, message ts, thread ts, nonce, expiry — code-owned constant, proposed 24h), key still the Connection's BotToken secret. The failure-notice render path attaches the signed Retry block only when the category is retryable and the signing credential loads; no key or non-retryable category means text-only (design B, C; part of the 'Retry action SHALL be signed' requirement).
acceptanceCriteria: Each retryable category (runner-unavailable, runner-lost, report-timeout, timeout/deadline, transport, rate-limit) attaches the signed Retry control as the only recovery control on the notice; input/configuration/permission, category-less, unknown, and legacy failures render text-only — matrix unit tests covering every classification branch
Retryability is decided from the authoritative category alone: a test with transient-sounding failure text ('timeout', 'unavailable') but a non-retryable category asserts no Retry control is attached

The mohist_retry_turn value binds session/input/turn identity, actor and initiator Slack user ids, connection id, team id, conversation id, message ts, thread ts, unique nonce, and a bounded expiry; signature is HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical payload with the Connection BotToken key and verifies in constant time — creation/verification unit tests
A Connection whose signing credential cannot be loaded renders the readable text notice with no Retry control — test

The canonical-form + HMAC + FixedTimeEquals helpers are extracted and shared; Stop creation and verification now route through the shared implementation with all existing Stop spec suites green (no behavior change)
Next-step copy per failure class (retryable / fix-then-resent / inspect-timeline) is rendered on the notice and asserted by tests
tasks.output: SlackFailureRetryPolicy classifier, shared Slack action-signing helper (Stop migrated onto it), SlackRetryActionPayload + mohist_retry_turn action id with 24h expiry constant, Retry block attachment in the failure-notice render path, and unit/spec tests for the matrix, signing, and attachment
tasks.notes: Click handling lands in T-006 within the same change; until then mohist_retry_turn clicks fall through SlackTurnControlService.HandleAsync's existing unknown-action handling — no release boundary ever carries a live-but-unhandled control. Confirm the exact lifetime constant (design Open Question proposes 24h) during implementation.

tasks.title: Durable retry-operation store, terminal-state validation, and retry-keyed root re-launch
tasks.description: Create the SlackRetryOperationStore with its own additive EF Core migration (SlackRetryOperations: unique action_key, unique retry_dispatch_key slack-retry:{connectionId}:{failedSessionId}:{failedTurnId}, target kind root|followup with failed ids, pre-minted attempt identities, pending/dispatching/applied/failed state, outcome, recovery lease, timestamps) and a Server-side retry execution service that validates the failed target against authoritative session state before any side effect, classifying it as exactly accepted / already_applied / stale / unavailable (root vs threaded derived from the failed turn's Job binding). For accepted root targets the service pre-mints fresh session/input/turn ids deterministically from the retry key (AgentLaunchCoordinatorCodec.StableToken scheme), commits the operation row pending, then re-launches through the shared IAgentLauncher.LaunchConnectionAsync boundary with an explicit idempotency-key override (default key unchanged for ordinary launches), copying provenance from the failed input, re-binding accepted attachments with availability re-check, and rebinding the thread/current-session routing mapping to the fresh session (design E, F, H; also requirements 'root request SHALL re-launch with fresh identities', 'validated before dispatch', 'immutable history', 'context-bound').
acceptanceCriteria: The SlackRetryOperations migration is applied at startup by DatabaseInitializer per db-migrations.md authoring rules, and a committed row captures action key, retry dispatch key, target, pre-minted identities, pending state, and recovery lease — migration + store round-trip tests

Terminal-state validation reports exactly one of accepted / already_applied / stale / unavailable against authoritative session state: still-failed un-retried resolvable targets are accepted; a target with an existing retry operation reports already_applied; a no-longer-failed target reports stale; an unresolvable session/input/turn reports unavailable with nothing dispatched — one test per result

A root retry re-launches with a new Session, initial Input, and Turn distinct from the failed attempt, under the retry-specific idempotency key, through the same LaunchConnectionAsync boundary a CLI/Web surface would call (no Slack-only dispatch path) — test

Re-processing the same retry under its key resolves to the same pre-minted identities rather than a second launch, and a conflicting payload under the same key is rejected as an idempotency conflict by coordinator fencing — tests

Commit precedes dispatch: the operation row is durably committed pending before any execution side effect, and a forced commit failure aborts the retry with an explicit outcome and zero side effect — test
The failed attempt's session/input/turn records remain unchanged as immutable history, and the fresh attempt executes against the same Connection and conversation — tests
The thread session mapping (channel) or current-session mapping (DM) is rebound to the fresh session idempotently, and a racing ordinary follow-up is never lost — test
Ordinary launches keep today's default idempotency key and existing launch-coordinator suites stay green (regression)
tasks.output: SlackRetryOperationStore + EF migration (Infrastructure/Data/Migrations), retry execution service with terminal-state validation and commit-before-dispatch orchestration, IAgentLauncher/AgentLaunchCoordinatorGrain idempotency-key override with retry-keyed pre-minted ids, mapping rebind, and server spec tests under Specs/Sessions or Specs/Slack
tasks.notes: Independent of the presentation tasks (T-001/T-002): the store and validation operate on durable session state, not on the notice. UNIQUE(action_key) plus UNIQUE(retry_dispatch_key) make concurrency converge structurally: a concurrent first-click insert race is decided by the single-row insert; losers re-read and return the winner's recorded outcome. Attachment re-binding re-verifies availability at click time (design Open Question, proposed answer).

tasks.title: Force-new-turn threaded retry in the original session
tasks.description: Extend AcceptFollowupCommand with a force-new-turn admission mode that bypasses ChooseFollowupTurnForAssignment entirely: it always creates its own new Turn (queued when another turn is executing or queued) and never attaches the input to an existing turn, while ordinary message admission keeps today's steer/new-turn behavior. The retry follow-up carries the retry idempotency key, pre-minted input/turn ids derived from it, and provenance copied from the failed input (identical member/message/thread facts; the clicking actor is recorded on the retry operation, not forged into provenance), commits into the SlackRetryOperationStore before dispatch, and dispatches through a turn-targeted variant of BeginNextFollowupDispatchAsync exposed by the session grain and driven by AgentSessionFollowupDispatcher so the retry never depends on FIFO position (design G).
acceptanceCriteria: Force-new-turn admission always creates its own new Turn — queued behind any executing or queued turn — and never joins, merges with, or extends another turn; domain tests cover the idle, queued, and executing cases

Ordinary follow-up admission (steer/new-turn decision via ChooseFollowupTurnForAssignment) is unchanged for ordinary messages, and an unrelated queued or executing follow-up continues its own admission untouched — regression tests
The retry follow-up is admitted under the retry idempotency key with pre-minted input/turn ids; re-processing resolves to the same ids instead of a second turn — test
The turn-targeted dispatch variant dispatches exactly the retry's turn regardless of FIFO position; the retry never rides an unrelated follow-up's dispatch — test
The retry stays bound to the original Session and conversation, the failed turn's records remain immutable, and the operation row is committed before the targeted dispatch — tests
tasks.output: AcceptFollowupCommand force-new-turn admission mode (Sessions/Domain + AgentSessionGrain), turn-targeted BeginNextFollowupDispatchAsync variant (AgentSessionGrain.FollowupDispatch.cs + AgentSessionFollowupDispatcher), threaded retry orchestration wired into the T-003 store/service, and domain/spec tests
tasks.notes: Provenance copying preserves reply anchoring and thread binding; identity is copied from the failed input, never synthesized from the clicking actor.

tasks.title: Fixed-key retry recovery reminder grain
tasks.description: Add a SlackRetryRecoveryGrain mirroring the SlackOutboxDispatcherGrain pattern: fixed string key (rogue activations ignored), persistent reminder, startup activation service, and a post-commit poke API the click path will call (T-006). The reminder scans SlackRetryOperations for committed-but-pending rows whose recovery lease expired, claims them optimatively, and resumes them exactly once — root operations re-drive the launch coordinator, threaded operations re-drive the turn-targeted follow-up dispatch, and an interrupted mapping rebind is completed — relying on the execution layer's idempotency keys as the true exactly-once fence (design I).
acceptanceCriteria: The grain activates only under its fixed string key (rogue activations ignored), registers a persistent reminder, is activated at startup by an activation service, and exposes a post-commit poke — unit tests mirroring the outbox-dispatcher suites

A crash between operation commit and dispatch resumes on restart via the reminder and dispatches the pre-minted attempt exactly once, without minting a second attempt — crash-recovery test (root and threaded variants)
The recovery lease prevents two in-flight drivers from duplicating presentation work; an expired lease allows takeover — lease-contention test
Resumption uses only the durable record (pre-minted identities, target kind, state) and re-enters the existing operation rather than creating a new one — test

Execution idempotency keys (coordinator key / follow-up key) remain the exactly-once fence; the lease is presentation-only — asserted by a test where the lease expires mid-drive without duplicating the attempt
tasks.output: SlackRetryRecoveryGrain + activation service (Infrastructure/Slack), recovery-lease claiming and resume logic for root and threaded operations, post-commit poke API, and reminder/recovery spec tests
tasks.notes: Fixed-key sweep is the established pattern (SlackOutboxDispatcherGrain, EventDispatcherGrain); per-operation reminder grains were rejected in the design as unbounded churn.

tasks.title: Retry click handling: verification, re-authorization, dispatch wiring, and durable outcome presentations
tasks.description: Dispatch mohist_retry_turn at the existing /interactions boundary (SlackInteractionRoutes) into a Retry branch of SlackTurnControlService that verifies in order: parse + constant-time signature + version/discriminator, expiry, context binding against the live Connection and click envelope, actor equality with the payload-bound actor, nonce consumption in the provider inbox under message identity action:{nonce} with a new Retry route kind (a consumed nonce re-enters the recorded operation), and current authorization via SlackConnectionAccessDecider.EvaluateAsync — a bound actor alone is not authorization. Accepted clicks invoke the T-003/T-004 retry execution service, poke the T-005 recovery grain, and update the failure notice through the existing outbox to acknowledge the retry, project the new attempt's working state, and include a newly signed Stop control via CreateStopActionAsync; rejected, expired, stale, unavailable, already-applied, and replayed clicks remove or replace the obsolete Retry control with the explicit outcome text, converging on one presentation mutation via ActionDispatchRef, with every click audited (design D, E, J).
acceptanceCriteria: mohist_retry_turn is dispatched at the existing /interactions endpoint with no new adapter-facing endpoint; the verification chain (unparseable value, tampered signature, unsupported version, expired action, context mismatch, actor mismatch) rejects each case with an explicit user-visible outcome and zero execution side effect — one test per case

A payload-bound actor whom the current Connection access policy no longer authorizes gets an explicit unauthorized outcome with no side effect — lost-access test (allowlist change after notice render)

A replayed interaction (consumed nonce, Slack redelivery, adapter failover under a different lease) re-enters the recorded retry operation and returns its recorded outcome, re-projecting the presentation if needed rather than returning only a duplicate receipt — tests

An accepted click starts exactly one fresh attempt — root via the retry-keyed re-launch, threaded via force-new-turn follow-up — and repeat deliveries of that click's outcome start no additional attempt — end-to-end test

The accepted outcome updates the notice in place (outbox UserAction chat.update at the notice message) to acknowledge the retry, project the new attempt's working state, and include a signed Stop control when the new attempt is stoppable — test
Rejected / stale / unavailable / already-applied outcomes remove or replace the obsolete Retry control on the notice through existing outbox durability and retry semantics — test
Repeated delivery of the same click converges on one presentation mutation keyed on ActionDispatchRef — convergence test
Every Retry click is audited with workspace, conversation, actor, target, and outcome, matching the existing Slack control audit shape

A retried attempt that fails again flows through the ordinary terminal pipeline to a new failure notice with a fresh Retry action on new attempt identities, without violating the unique-key rule — chained-retry test
tasks.output: SlackInteractionRoutes retry dispatch, SlackTurnControlService Retry branch with full verification/authorization chain, SlackProviderInboxRouteKinds.Retry, accepted/rejected outcome presentations via the outbox, post-commit poke wiring, audit records, and Specs/Slack click-matrix suites
tasks.notes: This task closes the loop between the action capability and the execution capability; after it lands, a failed retryable Slack turn is recoverable end-to-end in-conversation. Stop behavior, Agent reply ownership, and Workflow recovery semantics must remain unchanged (regression suites).

tasks.title: Adapter pass-through contract coverage (TypeScript and Go)
tasks.description: Add contract tests proving both adapters treat Retry as pure pass-through with no production code changes: the TypeScript adapter (packages/mohist-slack) forwards the mohist_retry_turn action id and signed value unchanged in the interaction envelope under the existing lease identity, acknowledges Slack promptly exactly as for Stop, and delivers Server-provided failure-notice blocks, Retry blocks, and outcome-update blocks without rewriting, filtering, or interpreting them; the Go transport port (packages/go/mohist-slack) gets the equivalent InteractionEnvelope forwarding and blocks pass-through coverage (design L).
acceptanceCriteria: TypeScript contract tests (adapter-events/transport suites) assert mohist_retry_turn action id and signed value are forwarded unchanged under the lease identity with prompt acknowledgement and no Retry-specific processing — vitest green
TypeScript delivery tests assert Server-provided notice blocks, Retry blocks, and outcome-update blocks are delivered byte-unchanged — vitest green
Go contract tests (serverapi_test.go) assert the InteractionEnvelope forwards the Retry action id/value unchanged and Server blocks pass through — go test green
Both adapters gain no new action grammar, endpoint, authorization logic, or persisted state — verified by review of the diff showing test-only changes
Existing Stop forwarding and delivery contract suites remain green (regression)
tasks.output: New/extended contract tests in packages/mohist-slack/src (adapter-events, adapter-delivery, transport suites) and packages/go/mohist-slack/serverapi_test.go; zero production adapter code changes
tasks.notes: Depends transitively on the finalized action grammar (T-002) and outcome block shapes (T-001, T-006). The adapters already forward arbitrary actionId/actionValue under the lease identity, so this is coverage only.
